sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Ossining different from other Westchester towns?
sections.html:
Ossining is a Hudson River town with two incorporated villages inside it, so the office that handles your permits and taxes depends on where the house sits. The town contains the Village of Ossining and part of Briarcliff Manor, plus an unincorporated area outside both villages (Wikipedia). The Town of Ossining Building Department has jurisdiction only in that unincorporated area, so a house inside a village goes to the village for permits.

The town covers 15.74 square miles, and 4.16 of those are water. The Hudson River bounds it on the west and the Croton River on the north. Sing Sing Correctional Facility, opened in 1826, is the best known landmark, and the village took the Ossining name in 1901 so goods made locally would not be confused with prison-made items.

Public schools belong to the Ossining Union Free School District, which runs Ossining High School, Anne M. Dorner Middle School and four elementary schools: Roosevelt, Claremont, Brookside and Park. Put the school district on every document, because the state disclosure form asks for it.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Ossining homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimated 39,964 residents on July 1, 2025, down 0.2 percent from the April 2020 base, and counted 13,711 households for 2020 to 2024. The owner-occupied rate is 62.8 percent, the median owner-occupied value is $552,900 and median gross rent is $2,203 (QuickFacts).

  • Median household income: $125,539 in 2024 dollars
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $3,774
  • Mean travel time to work: 36.5 minutes
  • Residents living in the same house a year earlier: 89.5 percent

With 37.6 percent of the population Hispanic or Latino and 40.4 percent of residents aged five and up speaking a language other than English at home, a listing or offer letter that is also available in Spanish can reach more buyers.

sections.h2: How does the 2025 reappraisal affect an Ossining sale?
sections.html:
The 2025 assessment roll followed a town reappraisal, so a buyer comparing your assessment with neighbors is looking at relatively fresh numbers. The town's project page says Tyler Technologies was hired to help with the work, and data collectors wore yellow vests and carried ID badges while they visited properties (Town of Ossining).

The same page notes that the town updates its assessment records every year. Ask the Assessor's Office, at 16 Croton Avenue, 3rd Floor, for your property record card before you list. Check it for errors such as a wrong bedroom count or an unrecorded addition, and raise them informally, since the town says you may contact the office at any time to discuss an assessment. Office hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, with Friday closing at 3:15 pm from July 1 through September 1 for every town office except the Town Clerk.

Scam warnings matter too. The town's home page cautions residents about callers who claim to be the Building Department and ask for extra application funds. If a message pressures you, contact the department using the details on the town website.

sections.h2: When is Grievance Day in the Town of Ossining?
sections.html:
Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, which matches the state tax department's note that Westchester town boards of assessment review meet on that day (tax.ny.gov). In 2026 the board sat on June 16 from 4:30 pm to 8:30 pm, and that date has passed. The next one falls in June 2027.

Ossining calendar itemWhen
Valuation dateJuly 1 of the prior year
Taxable status day and exemption filing deadlineMay 1
Tentative assessment roll publishedJune 1
Grievance DayThird Tuesday in June
Final assessment roll publishedSeptember 15

Source: Town of Ossining grievance procedures.

The town advises filing the state complaint form, bringing a grievance questionnaire and offering evidence of market value such as a recent purchase price, comparable sales or an appraisal. Your ability to pay or how much you use public services does not count. The board's decision arrives by September 15, and an owner of a one, two or three family home who lives there can then file a Small Claims Assessment Review without a lawyer.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record and tax a deed in Westchester County?
sections.html:
The Westchester County Clerk lists a $45 statutory recording fee for a deed, $5 for each written side of a page, $5 to file Form TP-584 on residential property and $125 to file the RP-5217 transfer report. The clerk's own example is a three-page residential deed in one municipality, which comes to $190 (Westchester County Clerk).

The state transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of the price, rounded up to the next $500. At the town's median owner-occupied value of $552,900, the rounded price is $553,000, which is 1,106 units and $2,212. The seller normally pays it, while the 1 percent mansion tax at $1 million or more falls on the buyer (tax.ny.gov).

  • Fees for a submission are calculated in the county's Property Records Electronic Portal.
  • Transfer tax must be paid by ACH, certified check, bank check, attorney escrow check or a check from a vendor on the clerk's approved list.
  • Credit cards work for ordinary fees up to $500 but not for taxes.

Title companies and attorneys usually handle all of this, so ask who files the deed and when.

sections.h2: What disclosure does a seller owe in Ossining?
sections.html:
A seller of a one to four family home must complete a property condition disclosure statement and deliver it before the buyer signs a binding contract (Real Property Law 462). For a town bounded by the Hudson and Croton rivers, the flood questions deserve attention.

The form asks whether any part of the property is in a FEMA floodplain, whether flood insurance exists, whether you filed a flood claim, and whether the building ever took in water from rainfall, storm surge, tidal inundation or river overflow. It also asks about leased or shared areas, septic or public sewer, a sump pump, the roof, and any radon testing. A seller who learns something that makes an earlier statement wrong must deliver a revised statement before title passes. The law keeps as-is sales available, but it does not remove the form.

If your house has an unpermitted deck, shed or finished basement, ask the Building Department or your village whether a permit can still be closed out. Questions about certificates of occupancy appear on the form itself.

sections.h2: Is a cash offer a fit for an Ossining house?
sections.html:
It can be, particularly when the house needs work that a retail buyer's inspection would flag. A direct cash purchase skips lender underwriting, so the schedule depends on title, payoff letters and the recording steps above. If the owner has died, ask an attorney which estate documents the title company will need before a deed is signed.

Before accepting any offer, request it in writing, find out who pays the transfer tax and recording, and verify that the buyer can close on the date promised. The Assessor's Office can answer questions about your assessment and exemptions that no buyer can.

faqs.q: Does the Town of Ossining Building Department cover the village?
faqs.a: No. The town's own site says the department has jurisdiction only in the unincorporated area outside the village limits. If your house is in the Village of Ossining or the Briarcliff Manor part of the town, contact that village for permits and certificates.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Ossining assessment?
faqs.a: File on or before the third Tuesday in June, the town's Grievance Day. The 2026 hearing on June 16 has passed. The tentative roll is published June 1, and you must file with the Board of Assessment Review before you can seek any further remedy.

faqs.q: How much is the state transfer tax on an Ossining sale?
faqs.a: It is $2 for every $500 of the price, rounded up. A $553,000 sale produces $2,212. The seller pays that tax unless the contract says otherwise, and the buyer pays the extra 1 percent mansion tax only on residences priced at $1 million or more.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer the property condition disclosure?
faqs.a: Yes, for a one to four family house. The signed statement must reach the buyer or the buyer's agent before the buyer signs a binding contract, and a copy signed by both sides is attached to the contract. Condominiums and cooperative apartments fall outside the definition.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for an Ossining house?
faqs.a: With the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. Its fee schedule lists $45 plus $5 per page for a deed, and cover pages and transfer forms are prepared through the county's online records portal. The clerk's phone line for fee questions is listed on the fee page as (914) 995-3094.
